subject: Follow-up: LumenHealth latency requirements and performance proof window
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: LumenHealth latency requirements and performance proof window

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we promised to surface: 

Summary from our side
- Primary KPI: minimize end-to-end response time for your clinical inference path (user prompt -> model output).
- You called out target ranges rather than hard SLAs: 95th percentile (95th) and 99th percentile (99th) across production-like traffic.

Clarifying asks we need from Lumen to size a hosted qualification run
1) Traffic envelope: expected RPS during peak sustained windows (and burst behavior). You mentioned ~200–300 RPS peak — please confirm sustained vs. burst.
2) Typical prompt length distribution: mean tokens and 90th token length. We need a sample CSV of 100 representative payloads if possible.
3) Streaming requirements: is partial token streaming (token-by-token) required end-to-end, or is streaming just a UX nicety? Are you relying on client-side playback for progressive display?
4) Concurrency and session semantics: how many concurrent conversations must preserve KV cache (per-user session pinning)? You mentioned 60–80 concurrent sessions.
5) Current provider baseline: can you attach the recent latency samples (p50/p95/p99) and sample RPS logs?

Immediate next steps (proposed by Redwood)
- We’ll propose a 72-hour proof window using hosted API with a mirrored traffic generator to approximate your envelope. We’ll run two flavors: quantized model variant (lower cost) and full-precision for parity.
- Deliverables: p50/p95/p99 breakdown by route + streaming latency breakdown (time-to-first-byte vs. final-token).
- Risk callouts: warm/cold KV cache behavior, tail effects on long prompts, and interaction with your ingress (edge/proxy) termination.

Attachments: Lumen_SLO_matrix.xlsx (placeholder for your confirmation), current-provider-latency-sample.csv (please send if available).

Thanks — I’ll circle back with a proposed test window and a short runbook.

— Elliot
Elliot Price
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@lumenhealth.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@lumenhealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: LumenHealth latency requirements and performance proof window

Elliot — thanks for the clear recap, that aligns with our internal notes. Answers inline: 

1) Traffic envelope
- Peak: sustained 220 RPS for a 30-minute window during business hours; occasional spikes to ~420 RPS for <2 minutes. For the qualification we can provide a 30-minute sustained trace and a 2-minute burst trace.

2) Prompt length distribution
- Mean user prompt: ~60 tokens; 90th percentile ~180 tokens. We’ll attach 100 representative prompts (we’ll scrub PHI first).

3) Streaming requirement
- We do require streaming for the main clinical triage UI: we expect time-to-first-token to be <120ms ideally for user experience, and progressive token delivery. If streaming degrades tail stability we need a fallback to buffered full-response.

4) Concurrency/session semantics
- Session model: per-patient session affinity required for KV cache retention. Target concurrent pinned sessions: 75.

5) Baseline artifacts
- Attach current-provider-latency-sample.csv (we’ll send this in a follow-up with the scrubbed prompt set).

SLO targets (what we’re hoping to validate)
- p95 end-to-end (user -> final token): <= 250 ms for typical prompts (60 tokens).
- p99 end-to-end: <= 600 ms.
- Throughput: sustain 220 RPS with 2m burst to 420 RPS.

We’re generally open to Redwood’s proposed 72-hour window. Can you call out what telemetry you’ll need on our side (headers, LB configs, sample auth tokens)? Also include a short rollback/fallback plan if tails regress.

— Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Ops | LumenHealth

---
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@lumenhealth.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: LumenHealth latency requirements and performance proof window

Thanks Maya — very helpful. Technical plan + minimal telemetry checklist below. I’m a sales-eng, I’ll own the run coordination and engineering handoff.

Run structure (proposed)
- Day 0: shadow dry-run with synthetic traffic (no tokens) to validate ingress, routing and request shaping. Verify our generator can replay the 30-min sustained and 2-min burst shapes.
- Day 1–3: 72-hour qualification where we gradually increase load to the stated envelope and run two model variants (quantized and full-precision).
- Observability: we’ll capture time-to-first-byte (TTFB), time-to-first-token (for streaming), token cadence, p50/p95/p99 for both TTFB and end-to-end final-token.

Telemetry we need from Lumen
- Ingress headers if you use user-session pinning (we need the session id header key so we can pin requests consistently).
- Sample auth-token for the test harness (revokable).
- A small set of LB/edge configuration details: idle timeouts, keepalive, max connections per upstream.

Success/failure criteria
- Success: p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 600ms for the representative prompt mix for at least two 30-minute windows during the run. Also streaming TTFB <= 120ms for >=90% of requests that require streaming.
- Failure: persistent p99 regressions outside the target for >30 minutes or repeated unrecoverable errors during burst >5% error rate.

Risk mitigations / fallback options
- Warm KV cache pre-fill: we’ll seed a warmed cache for a 30-minute warm period to match production behavior.
- Canary routing + fallback: during the test we recommend 5–10% of real traffic (if you prefer) or a purely synthetic mirror. If tails regress we can revert to the incumbent model variant or switch to buffered responses while we triage.

Attachments: runbook_template.md (internal), test-traffic-shapes.json (synthetic shapes).

I’ll sync with infra to reserve slots for the 72-hour window — proposed start: Mon 28 Jul 2025 02:00 UTC. Elliot — can you confirm commercial signoff and who in procurement to loop for the test-access token?

— Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jul 2025 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: LumenHealth latency requirements and performance proof window

Looping in to confirm infra reservations and a small operational ask: 

- Infra capacity: I’ve reserved a dedicated hosted pool and configured an autoscale ceiling to cover 500 RPS bursts for the qualification. We’ll enable the quantized variant and full-precision variant runs on separate nodes to avoid noisy neighbor interference.
- Observability hooks: enable request-id echo and a short-lived API key. Camila — please share the runbook steps and we’ll pre-provision the dashboards (trace/span level logs + per-route tokenized latency).

Operational note for Lumen: we can accept streamed responses over chunked-transfer-encoding or HTTP/2 trailers — confirm which your UI supports. If you prefer, we’ll instrument both and provide a compatibility matrix.

Happy to take a 15-min ops handoff next week to finalize the start time.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
